terms.grammar: phrase: diēs, feminine of a fixed day, with the participle of praestituere
evidence: Cic. Verr. 2.1.148: diem praestituit operī faciundō (Lewis & Short)
terms.comment: Lewis & Short: praestituere, to determine or appoint beforehand; to set a deadline is diem praestituere. Diēs is feminine of a day fixed or appointed.

evidence: M-O s.v. deadline, after Erasmus, Colloquia: ad diem praescrīptum

phrases.english: he set a deadline for doing the work

sources: Lewis & Short: praestituo · Lewis & Short: praescribo · Lewis & Short: dies
Morgan–Owens, Adumbratio: s.v. deadline.
